CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female with a past medical history significant for coronary artery disease with prior stenting, herniated disc, and prior carpal tunnel release presenting for her annual examination. Regarding her herniated disc, she reports doing very well since steroid injection several months ago with no back pain or limitations in movement. Her carpal tunnel release was performed a couple of years ago, and she has returned to work with no recurrent issues, full range of motion, and no numbness or tingling in her hands. Regarding her coronary artery disease, she reports new onset of chest pain over the last month. The chest pain is described as a burning sensation, located in the middle of her chest, occurs with ambulation, and resolves with rest. She denies chest pain at rest. She reports the pain occurs approximately three times per week. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. She also reports nasal congestion from seasonal allergies due to pollen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for chest pressure and nasal congestion. Negative for lower extremity edema, muscle aches, fever, chills, shortness of breath, nausea, and vomiting.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
Herniated disc
Prior carpal tunnel release

MEDICATIONS
Aspirin
Toprol

ALLERGIES
Pollen

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is currently working.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygen saturation normal.
Cardiovascular: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur noted (previously appreciated). No carotid bruits.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally.
Extremities: No lower extremity edema. Healed surgical scars noted on right wrist.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram (prior year): Left ventricular ejection fraction 45%, mild mitral regurgitation.
EKG: Stable, reflecting prior coronary artery disease with no new changes.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel release - Patient doing well with full functional recovery and return to work. No further intervention needed at this time. Patient instructed to report if recurrent symptoms develop.

2. Herniated disc - Patient reporting good pain control and functional status post steroid injection. No further steroid injection or physical therapy recommended at this time. Patient instructed to report if recurrent symptoms develop.

3. Coronary artery disease with recurrent chest pain - Continue current medications including aspirin and Toprol. Ordered cardiac stress test to evaluate for possible additional blockages. Ordered lipid panel. Initiated Crestor 20 mg once daily. Patient to follow up with scheduling for stress testing.
